status: Contained design preview; not an implemented Plymouth/SDDM sequence
production_completion: Actual boot/display-manager readiness takes precedence. Never delay boot or authentication to complete this preview timeline.

digits.source_policy: Public theme calibration/default only. Never read an unauthenticated user's home directory, per-user state file or session bus.
digits.production_alternative: Omit digits if they imply a user's confirmed private worldline. Session-specific divergence appears only after authentication.

stages.label: Signal emergence
stages.visual: A few low-contrast light traces appear on graphite; no repeated scanline flash.

stages.label: Emblem assembly
stages.visual: Trace segments resolve into the existing geometric emblem. No new logo is selected.

stages.label: Calibration
stages.visual: One brief provisional digit treatment beneath the mark, then a stable public theme value.

stages.label: Quiet identification
stages.visual: The mark settles and temporary traces/digits recede. No looping decorative gauges.

stages.label: Readiness handoff
stages.visual: Carry the background/mark alignment into the greeter only when ready. Authentication controls remain immediately available.
stages.cue: Optional post-login session-ready cue only, subject to per-user preferences, global mute and rate limiting.

reduced.visual: Short fade or static mark. No assembly travel, rolling digits or scanning.

off.visual: Static emblem and genuine status/password/question controls; immediate handoff when ready.

integration_boundaries.early_boot: Plymouth script theme in initramfs; must preserve status, password, question and text/TTY fallback.
integration_boundaries.greeter: A separately qualified SDDM theme using its supported authentication proxy/models; no session-service shortcut around authentication.
integration_boundaries.session: User worldline service applies current state after authenticated startup; no delayed boot cinematic replay.
integration_boundaries.sound: No initramfs audio dependency. Optional session-ready cue belongs to an authenticated user session and never blocks startup.
